record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
record.context_brief: Intrinsic meaning of the corrected form-to-section map
record.original_question: What is the geometric meaning of the construction that sends a smooth differential k-form on a Riemannian manifold, together with the Levi-Civita connection, to two global sections J+ and J− of the chiral de Rham complex using local expressions built from the inverse metric, Christoffel symbols, Bessel-polynomial coefficients, ∂γ terms, and the local generators e_i^±? Equivalently, can the corrected normally ordered formula that glues local expressions into global chiral-de Rham sections be characterized by a more intrinsic geometric construction?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold with Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$ and Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^{i}_{jk}$, and let $\Omega^{ch}_M$ denote the chiral de Rham complex of $M$ (the sheaf of vertex superalgebras locally generated, on a coordinate chart $U$ with coordinates $x^i$, by even fields $\gamma^i, a_i$ and odd fields $b_i, c^i$ subject to the standard OPE relations of the $bc$–$\beta\gamma$ system). On a chart $U$ introduce the local odd generators
$$e_i^{\pm} \;=\; b_i \;\pm\; g_{ij}\,c^j .$$
For a smooth $k$-form $\omega \in C^\infty(M,\Lambda^k T^*M)$ written locally as $\omega = \sum \omega_{i_1\dots i_k}\,dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k}$, define two local sections by the normally ordered expressions
$$J^{\pm}(\omega) \;=\; \sum \omega_{i_1\dots i_k}\bigl(\gamma\bigr)\,:\!e_{i_1}^{\pm}\cdots e_{i_k}^{\pm}\!:\;+\;(\text{correction terms}),$$
where the correction terms are constructed from the inverse metric $g^{ij}$, the Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^{i}_{jk}$, derivatives $\partial\gamma^{l}$, and coefficients given by Bessel polynomials, in such a way that each increase of the form-degree by two requires the insertion of an additional term of the schematic shape $\Gamma^{k}_{\ell m}\,g^{jm}\,\partial\gamma^{\ell}$. Suppose these local expressions glue into two globally well-defined embeddings of sheaves
$$J^{\pm}\colon \Lambda^{\bullet} T^*M \;\hookrightarrow\; \Omega^{ch}_M .$$

Problem. Provide an intrinsic geometric (coordinate-free) characterization of the maps $J^{\pm}$. Equivalently, identify a natural geometric construction—formulated solely in terms of $(M,g,\nabla)$ and standard tensorial/vertex-algebraic operations—that produces the corrected normally ordered local formulas above and explains why the specific Bessel-polynomial coefficients and $\partial\gamma$ corrections are exactly those required for global gluing into $\Omega^{ch}_M$.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search returns the foundational works on the chiral de Rham complex on Riemannian manifolds (Ekstrand–Heluani–Källén–Zabzine, Heluani–Zabzine, and the original Malikov–Schechtman–Vaintrob construction) and follow-ups on twisted/exotic CDR and T-duality, but no source explicitly identifies an intrinsic coordinate-free geometric characterization of the corrected form-to-section maps $J^{\pm}$ involving the Bessel-polynomial corrections and $\partial\gamma$ terms. The status of an intrinsic geometric description appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Chiral de Rham Complex on Riemannian Manifolds and Special Holonomy
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs N=1 (and enhanced) superconformal structures on the chiral de Rham complex from the Levi-Civita connection on a Riemannian manifold.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework in which the embeddings J± live but does not give an intrinsic geometric description of the corrected form-to-section maps.

status_evidence.title: Supersymmetry of the Chiral de Rham Complex
status_evidence.snippet: Heluani–Zabzine paper on superfield formulation of the chiral de Rham complex on smooth manifolds with metric.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the SUSY structure underlying the form-to-section maps but leaves open an intrinsic characterization of the corrections.

status_evidence.title: Chiral de Rham complex (Malikov–Schechtman–Vaintrob)
status_evidence.snippet: Original construction of the chiral de Rham complex as a sheaf of vertex algebras on a smooth manifold.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the ambient sheaf $\Omega^{ch}_M$ used in the problem.
